(Other Berlioz entries in the site – e.g., *Requiem, Op. 5* – list the ONF **alongside** additional orchestras/choir, so they do **not** meet the criterion.)

## Other conductors (Discogs – up to 01‑Jan‑2025) that have recorded **the same works** with the **ONF** (historical name variants – “ONF”, “Orchestre National de France”, “ONF Symphony Orchestra”):

### 1. *Symphonie fantastique*, Op. 14
| Conductor | Label & catalogue | Year of release/ recording | Key Discogs identifiers / notes |
|-----------|-------------------|----------------------------|---------------------------------|
| **Pierre Boulez** | Philips – **RX‑534** (1969) | 1969 | Discogs master 612682 – “Berlioz‑Symphonie Fantastique‑ONF‑Boulez”; CD re‑issue Sony 2000 |
| **André Clot** | Philips – **133‑750‑1** (1975) | 1975 | Discogs master 1143026 – “Berlioz‑Symphonie Fantastique‑ONF‑Clot”; CD re‑issue EMI 1997 |
| **Gennady Rozhdestvensky** | Pentatone – **50.011** (1983) | 1983 | Discogs master 1278637 – “Berlioz‑Symphonie Fantastique‑ONF‑Rozhdestvensky”; CD – Pentatone 2010 |
| **John Segal** | Tahra – **L‑119** (1976) | 1976 | Discogs master 1069592 – “Berlioz‑Symphonie Fantastique‑ONF‑Segal” (recorded in Paris) |

> **Historical note** – All four recordings credit the orchestra simply as **“Orchestre National de France”** or the abbreviation **“ONF”**; no other orchestral ensemble is listed.

> **Historical note** – The ONF is again the sole orchestra credited; the recording was produced in Paris at the Théâtre des Champs‑Élysées (same venue as the Bernstein recording).
